title: The Space Between the Boxes
question: Every panel is boxed now. How much of each panel is empty, between its boxes and inside them, at the screens and zoom levels the game is played on? Where does that space come from, and how much can the layout give back without hiding what a player uses?

asked.words: The prior effort created panels that leave a lot of "whitespace" between them in common zoom levels and screen sizes. Do an audit of that for the new report, and try to reduce that (before vs after) with a PR that we plan to merge with improvements.

report5.measured: counts only: TABS walked and SHOWN_WHEN run in node at the defaults; no pixels, no whitespace, no zoom levels
rules: 1. A box per thing, named once
every boxed tab (ticket 375); each box says its name once since ticket 392
2. Nesting by boxes alone, no dashed lines
kept in the boxed tabs; 🗺️ World design still draws dotted borders
3. Knolled: a grid, things of a kind the same size and lined up
the grids line their boxes up row by row, so a short box leaves a hole as tall as its row's tallest: see #rules
rows of 12 or more chips still wrap to 3 or more lines: extended to chip rows, see #rules
places as pictures, things as cards, castle themes as flags
7. Mirror the picture: every big tab a designer
all 20 tabs have a full screen (5 kinds)
the side panel sits on the line between one and two columns at common laptop zooms: 'every scale' now means every width and zoom
guarded by tabs167 and castlefs365; this report times nothing
steps: 1. The shared pieces: a box, the one-line row, the designer's shell
3. The castle's themes in one place, as flags
4. The bubble themes as three cards
ticket 375; its question, one on and off per theme, not settled either way
ticket 375 (12 tabs into boxes), ticket 488 (World design's side panel, Controls)
7. Tidy what the survey found stale
the stale comments went with ticket 285; not checked line by line here

amend: Things of a kind stay in rows (cards, theme cards, music cards, mixer strips, the castle designer's rooms, the world's order); different things, the boxes of a tab, are packed, each under the one above it, with no hole under a short one.
A row of chips is a row too: a short row of chips (8 or fewer) sits beside its label in a box wide enough, and a row that would take 3 lines or more is a chip box (the next rule).
The same at every width and zoom: the measure is the side panel at 1366x768 and 1920x1080 at 100%, 125% and 150%, the iPad both ways, and the phone, as tools/checks/knoll521.mjs measures it.
A grid has no more columns than boxes; what a full screen does not need for boxes, the game's card takes.
New: a long choice is one chip
Twelve or more text choices are one chip naming the current one, opening ticket 459's chip box (✖ and Escape close it); no dropdowns.
found: fitPic did not know the generic full screen's card
21-size-and-divider.js: in the 17 generic full screens the picture was not fitted to its card, so it was letterboxed (Figure 6). Fixed in the PR, the commit named "four panel bugs".
The bubble room's settings landed in a box named "🏰 the castles"
22-full-screen.js: the test picking the castles' box matched "room"; now it picks keys and groups that start with "castle". Same commit.
🔬 and ♿ stopped laying their switches out as chips
style.css: the rules for 🔬 Inspection's and ♿ Accessibility's chips did not reach through the designer's wrapper, one version after they shipped (0.0.315). Same commit.
Background's side panel had boxes but no grid
the boxes touched, with no gap between them; now a grid with the box gap, two to a row from 568 px. Same commit.
The bubble room's full screen is not the same twice

the only case where the three jobs differ (Figure 2's note): most likely because its bubbles move and the measure catches them in different places (not confirmed). Every other case, in every build, agrees to the pixel.
